public_rationale: The research establishes real reliability problems and limits on universal correctness. It does not settle the stronger attribution to architecture. A theorem showing that no computable model can answer every possible question correctly is not, by itself, proof of practical unreliability caused by LLM architecture. Research on training incentives supplies another relevant explanation. Neither support nor contradiction of the full claim is established.
limitations: Theoretical conclusions depend on their formal assumptions.
The empirical study covers particular models and tasks.
The September 2025 analysis is later evidence about mechanisms, not a contemporaneous observation at publication.

statement.excerpt: The problem here is that the architecture underlying Large Language Models is inherently unreliable.
statement.document_title: How To Argue With An AI Booster

from_speaker: the architecture underlying Large Language Models
our_interpretation: Although phrased as an observation, the claim attributes unreliability to architecture, so it is assessed as a causal claim.
The plain reading is that the design of general-purpose LLMs itself creates systematic factual errors or inconsistent answers.
Ordinary unreliability is stronger than merely failing to guarantee perfect answers to every possible question, but does not mean every answer is wrong.
criteria.support_condition: Reproducible studies establish systematic reliability failures and architectural analysis links those failures to the model design, beyond particular datasets, training incentives, or deployment choices.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Controlled evidence shows that the alleged systematic failures are removable within the same architecture, or that the proposed architectural explanation is false.

evidence.excerpt: larger and more instructable large language models may have become less reliable.
evidence.explanation: The experiments document persistent errors and sensitivity to phrasing across model families. They establish reliability problems, but do not isolate architecture as their necessary cause.

evidence.excerpt: we formalize the problem and show that it is impossible to eliminate hallucination in LLMs.
evidence.explanation: The formal result concerns computable models attempting to learn all computable ground-truth functions. That supports limits on universal correctness, but does not establish an ordinary unreliability rate or a defect specific to LLM architecture.

evidence.excerpt: Hallucinations need not be mysterious -- they originate simply as errors in binary classification.
evidence.explanation: This analysis identifies statistical limitations and incentives to guess, and proposes changes to evaluation incentives. It complicates an architecture-only explanation without demonstrating that all reliability problems can be eliminated.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Controlled studies separating architecture, data, training incentives, and abstention, together with a practical reliability criterion for general-purpose use.
